findings.title: Task 1 changes the duel golden’s canonical values
findings.claim: The proposed `flattenDuel` replaces the current short interior tail with the entire sector interior flatten, despite claiming the values and order are unchanged.
findings.evidence: plan L438-L450, L489-L510, L529-L532; src/renderer/src/sim/duel/hash.ts:L11-L16; src/renderer/src/sim/flatten.ts:L45-L50; tests/duelGolden.test.ts:L15-L24
findings.why: The value sequence changes immediately after the tactical values, so the unedited duel golden cannot pass.
findings.fix: Preserve the existing `flattenDuel` value sequence exactly. Store any additional interior state needed for continuation through a separately defined snapshot representation, and prove both with the golden and continuation tests.

findings.title: Snapshot validation misses tactical writer constraints
findings.claim: `validateDuelSnapshot` checks finite values and validates the interior, but accepts tactical values that module writers reject only after `loadDuelSnapshot` allocates a duel.
findings.why: For example, a missile presence value other than 0 or 1 with a recomputed header hash passes the validator and fails during restore. The promised validation before duel allocation is therefore incomplete.
findings.fix: Validate every tactical field’s bounds and slot invariants, including missile presence and empty-slot zeros, before calling `createDuel`; add a test that calls the validator on a rehashed invalid tactical value.

findings.title: The utility test bypasses the registered utility
findings.claim: The utility test constructs its own registry containing `duelMode`, so it passes even if `authorityHost.ts` fails to register the duel. It also does not perform the required utility-level capture and restore round trip.
findings.evidence: plan L2004-L2015, L2360-L2383; spec L215-L216; src/utility/authorityHost.ts:L11
findings.why: The test can pass for the wrong reason and cannot establish the stated utility acceptance criterion.
findings.fix: Exercise the built authority utility entry point with a duel initialize, start, capture, and restore sequence, then compare restored hashes; retain a sector identity check.

findings.title: The continuation proof does not establish its checkpoint conditions
findings.claim: The proof checks tick 6000 but never asserts that a missile is in flight, rooms are damaged, or a repair is active at that tick.
findings.why: If the scripted scenario changes, the test can still pass while no longer exercising the risky missile and repair fields at the checkpoint.
findings.fix: Assert those three conditions on the split state before capture, or select a split tick that satisfies them and assert it.

findings.title: The module migration leaves tactical cloning manual
findings.claim: The spec requires clone to derive from module fields and explicitly calls for ending the manual `cloneTactical`, but Task 1 leaves that function in place and tests it as the clone path. Only the omission of `create` is declared as a deviation.
findings.evidence: spec L118-L138; plan L49, L220-L222, L307-L402; src/renderer/src/sim/tactical/state.ts:L100-L110
findings.why: A future tactical field can enter the module snapshot and hash while still being omitted from the independently maintained clone.
findings.fix: Derive tactical cloning from the module fields in Task 1, or state and justify a staged exception to the spec and add a clone completeness check.
